name: Standing privileged access without a least-privilege basis
description: Administrative or production-data privilege is held on a standing basis without a documented role basis, without segregation-of-duties consideration, or without review; or elevation is nominally time-bounded while sessions are renewed indefinitely, producing standing privilege with the appearance of just-in-time control.

may_assert: That named identities hold privileged entitlements with no corresponding role definition or approval, where the privileged inventory has been supplied.
That elevation records show renewal patterns amounting to continuous privilege, where the elevation log evidences it.
That non-human identities hold privilege outside any review population.
must_not_assert: That standing privilege is prohibited. It is not; narrow, attributable, reviewed standing privilege can meet the objective.
That just-in-time elevation is required by SOC 2. It is a DriftGuard recommendation.
That privilege was misused. The observation concerns the entitlement, not any action taken with it.

escalates_to.when: Privileged entitlements were granted during the period outside the role model and no review detected them.

de_escalates_to.when: The privileged inventory omits non-human identities or a whole system, so the population cannot be assessed.

severity_factors.criterion_impact: Broad standing privilege makes any single account compromise an environment-wide compromise, which is what least privilege exists to bound.
severity_factors.pervasiveness: Two engineers with standing production access differs from an entire team holding administrator by default.
severity_factors.detectability: Detectable from a privileged entitlement inventory; frequently missed where service accounts are excluded from that inventory.
escalates_when: Privilege extends to production customer data
Conflicting entitlement combinations are held by one identity
Service accounts hold broader privilege than any human and are unreviewed
No review covers the privileged population at all
de_escalates_when: The population is small, named, and reviewed on a defined cadence
Elevation is genuinely time-bounded with justification captured
Privilege is scoped to a non-production environment holding no protected information

detection_signals.signal: Privileged inventory shows entitlements with no linked role definition or approval.
Elevation records show back-to-back renewals producing effectively continuous privilege.
Non-human identities holding privilege absent from the review population.
Respondent reports standing privilege that is not systematically reviewed.

auditor_impact: Auditors commonly examine the privileged population directly rather than sampling it, and probe whether each holder's role requires the privilege. Standing privilege that is reviewed and justified is routinely accepted.
customer_impact: A larger set of people than necessary can reach the customer's data at any time, widening the blast radius of any single credential compromise.
false_positive_guidance: Not a gap where standing privilege is narrow, attributable, and covered by a documented periodic review. The criterion concerns the objective, not the mechanism.
Not a gap for break-glass accounts that are vaulted, alerted on, and reviewed after use.
Not a gap where privilege is scoped to an environment holding no protected information; confirm against the system boundary first.
Small entities may legitimately have a high proportion of privileged staff. Assess against the role requirement, not against a headcount ratio.

source_refs.supports: Typical auditor treatment, severity factors, and detection approach.

notes: DriftGuard finding archetype. DriftGuard produces observations against it; only a service auditor issues findings.
